quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: An inattentive driver is a driver who:

options.text: Looks at things off the road or daydreams while driving.
Looks at a passenger while talking to them during driving.
Only watches the car in front of them.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by looking at passengers, searching for things in your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep scanning the road, checking your mirrors, and looking at your dashboard regularly. These safe habits will help you stay focused while driving.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Use different routes.
Drive the same way you do on dry roads.
Stay farther behind other cars.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. Your car will take longer to stop than it would on normal roads.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?

options.text: Whoever started moving last
The driver
Whoever is slower
The pedestrian

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: Drivers must let pedestrians cross at any intersection without a traffic light. This is true whether or not there is a crosswalk.

questions.question: What kinds of drugs can affect your driving ability?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can make it harder to drive. This includes illegal drugs and over-the-counter or prescription medicines. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area of the road:

options.text: You cannot see without turning your head.
Directly behind your car.
You can see in your rearview mirror.
You can see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are located to the sides of and behind your car.

questions.question: You come to an intersection blocked by traffic. You should:

options.text: Drive slowly until the traffic ahead moves.
Get as close as possible to the car ahead of you.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears so you can pass through.
Honk your horn to make cars move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears so you can pass through.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection if traffic is blocked on the other side and you cannot drive all the way through. Wait for traffic to clear so you do not block the intersection.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Keep driving at your current speed.
You must stop ahead.
Do not speed.
A traffic signal is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A traffic signal is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that there is a traffic signal ahead.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
Divided highway starts. Slow down to 35 mph.
Merge ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
Winding road ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right ahead. Slow down to 35 mph.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you the road curves to the right and shows the safe speed (35 mph). Slow down to this speed to drive safely through the curve.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Road work ahead.
The road curves left, then right.
The road curves right, then left.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the road curves to the right and then to the left. Slow down so you can safely drive through both curves.

questions.question: You are driving up a hill and approaching a heavy truck from behind. You should know that:

options.text: The truck may be going slower than the speed limit.
You may not be able to safely pass the truck.
You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Know that large trucks often go slower than the speed limit, especially on hills. Be careful when following a large truck. On hills with poor visibility, it is illegal to pass another car.

questions.question: What can you do from the center lane?

options.text: Make left turns.
Make U-turns.
Pass slow-moving traffic.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make left turns.
questions.explanation: The center lane is only for left turns. You cannot use it to pass other vehicles or drive straight through.

questions.question: What happens to a bicyclist who breaks traffic laws?

options.text: Nothing, because bicyclists don't have to follow traffic laws.
They can get a ticket.
They will always get a warning from police.
Their bicycle will be taken away.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can get a ticket.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists have the same rules and responsibilities as car drivers. Both can get tickets if they break traffic laws.

questions.question: What is true about drowsy drivers?

options.text: They should drink strong coffee to stay awake.
They may drive so badly they seem drunk.
They can stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.
They are usually only older drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may drive so badly they seem drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive very poorly, appearing to be drunk. Coffee, fresh air, and loud radio are not enough to keep a tired driver safe.

questions.question: What should you do at dusk or on overcast days?

options.text: Use your four-way flashers.
Use your parking lights.
Don't turn on any lights.
Turn on your headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming car or 500 feet of a car you are following. Always use low beams in bad weather.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through.
Turn right or left since the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop completely. After stopping, you can proceed when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: When should you slow down for a curve?

options.text: Before you enter the curve.
After you finish the curve.
In the middle of the curve.
Only if you see other cars coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Driving too fast can cause your tires to lose grip on the road.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: Potential speeds for the area.
The legal maximum or minimum speed allowed.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in bad conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The legal maximum or minimum speed allowed.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the maximum or minimum legal speed. These limits are for good conditions. You must slow down when weather or traffic is bad.

questions.question: When must you stop at an intersection?

options.text: When you see a flashing red light.
When you see a steady yellow light.
When you see a yellow arrow.
When you see a flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in bad weather?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Get closer to the car ahead of you.
Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car ahead of you.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, increase the distance between you and the car in front of you.

questions.question: What should you do if a car is coming toward you on the left and a bicyclist is on your right?

options.text: Pull onto the shoulder.
Drive between them.
Let the car pass first, then pass the bicycle.
Pass the bicycle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass first, then pass the bicycle.
questions.explanation: Deal with one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first. Then you can safely pass the bicyclist.

questions.question: How long must a driver practice on a probationary license?

options.text: One year.
Nine months.
Five months.
Eight weeks.

questions.correctAnswerText: One year.
questions.explanation: A driver with a probationary license must practice unsupervised driving for at least one year before getting a basic driver license. While you have a probationary license, you must follow all the rules and restrictions that apply to you.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?

options.text: Less dangerous.
No more or less dangerous.
More dangerous.
Easier on your eyes.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day. It is harder to see in the dark. Other drivers' headlights can blind you. More tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: Two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car approaching from the right has the right-of-way.
The car approaching from the left has the right-of-way.
The car in which the driver sounds his horn first has the right-of-way.
The car that is traveling the fastest has the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car approaching from the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, you must yield to a vehicle approaching from your right.

questions.question: What should you do if you are driving in another driver's blind spot?

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in someone else's blind spot. Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.

questions.question: When turning or changing lanes, what must you do?

options.text: Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.
Signal only if there is visible traffic.
Signal only when driving at night.
Signal only when driving in heavy traffic at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always signal your intentions, even when no visible traffic is present.
questions.explanation: Always signal when changing lanes, turning, or pulling away from a curb. Do not skip this step even if you do not see other traffic. Make it a habit to always signal.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery during rain?

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
The day after it rains.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain has stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain causes oil in the asphalt to rise to the surface. Hot weather makes this worse by bringing up more oil.

questions.question: What can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Allowing extra travel time.
Obeying posted speed limits.
Using proper turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: To prevent road rage, use proper turn signals, obey speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip. These habits help reduce conflict on the road.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but is not using emergency signals. What should you do?

options.text: Continue to drive in a normal manner.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Speed up to get out of its way.
Slow down, move as far to the right as possible, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to drive in a normal manner.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is not using its siren or flashing lights, you do not need to move out of its way. Continue driving normally.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is for one-way traffic only.
That due to upcoming roadwork, there is a detour to the right.
Slow down because the road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead changes direction at an extreme angle.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has a sharp turn. Slow down as you would when making a sharp turn at an intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly and sound your horn.
A bus stop is ahead.
You are entering a school's parking lot.
A school zone is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A school zone is ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you that a school zone is ahead. Slow down and watch for children.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Not cross the centerline.
Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the shoulder.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the oncoming traffic lane to complete your pass. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Slam on your brakes to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors several times each minute to notice tailgaters. If a car is following too close, slow down and let it pass. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: By looking in your side mirrors.
By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
By looking in your rearview mirror.
By staring straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: By turning your head and looking over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your car that mirrors cannot show. Check them by turning your head and looking over your shoulder.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving, as you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Check what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Drive at the same speed.
Slow down to give them room to pass safely and easily.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely and easily.
questions.explanation: When someone behind you wants to pass, slow down. This gives them more space to complete the pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: The most important thing about speed and curves is that you must:

options.text: Drive at the speed limit when entering the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's momentum can make it hard to turn. Slow down before entering a curve to stay in control.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for the conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Speeding is a major cause of crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely risky behavior.
Nothing to worry about.
As safe as driving under any other conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely risky behavior.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Staying focused on driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: A driver with a probationary license:

options.text: May use a hand-held cell phone while driving.
Must wear a seat belt, but passengers do not have to.
May not use a hands-free cell phone while driving.
May drive without a seat belt, though it is not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: May not use a hands-free cell phone while driving.
questions.explanation: Drivers with probationary licenses have restrictions. They cannot use hand-held or hands-free cell phones and must wear a seat belt. Drivers under 21 cannot drive between 11:01 p.m. and 5:00 a.m.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the roadway, you should:

options.text: Take no special action.
Honk your horn.
Pass the animal as close as possible.
Be very cautious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very cautious.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: What should you do to make sure your physical condition does not make you drive unsafely?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how any medicine you take affects your driving.
Only drive within what your body can handle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects how safely you can drive. You should know your limits and only drive when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign do?

options.text: Warns of hazards that are happening or might happen.
Tells drivers about school zones.
Tells drivers about public recreation areas.
Tells drivers about food and gas locations ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns of hazards that are happening or might happen.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of dangers on the road. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, two drivers arrive at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver can continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, give the right-of-way to the driver on your right if you both arrive at the same time. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on an interstate?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Always use cruise control.
Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots before changing lanes.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes or passing. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or bad weather.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before you enter the ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the ramp.
Keep your speed the same once on the ramp.
Pass slower cars on the ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until you are on the exit ramp.

questions.question: What can happen when you drink alcohol while taking drugs?

options.text: The effects of the drugs and alcohol get weaker.
The effects of both the drugs and alcohol get stronger.
It helps cure your illness.
It improves your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both the drugs and alcohol get stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can make both stronger. Driving after using either one is unsafe. Mixing them is even more dangerous.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
You cannot turn anymore and must go straight.
You still have the right-of-way to turn.
You do not have to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in that direction, but you must first let pedestrians and oncoming cars pass.

questions.question: What should you do while backing up?

options.text: Only use your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Check behind your car before backing up. Turn your head to look through the rear window. Children and small objects are hard to see from your seat. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is coming?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights. Pull to the right side of the road if you can. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn cars that you are entering.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge with traffic smoothly.
Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must give the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.
